observations.finding: One served FastAPI app is defined at apps/api/strikecast_api/main.py; core package owns API schemas and the runtime risk/model boundary.
Research and training trees contain separate ConvLSTM/model and trainer implementations from the served core; they are retained for experiments and are not interchangeable.
No canonical raw ERA5/LIS paired dataset builder exists. The guarded CLI is demo-only and strict prepared-data loader is not a provider adapter.
API rate limiter is process-local memory and does not protect a multi-worker deployment consistently.
Development launcher enables reload and binds 0.0.0.0; it must not be treated as production deployment.
No Git metadata is present in this checkout; commit-based provenance and working-tree diff cannot be verified.
ZIP inventory validates metadata/CRC without extraction; no canonical safe extraction utility is present. Any future extraction requires containment and expansion limits.
Python requirements are not a complete hash-locked environment; web app has package-lock.json. Dependency audit required.
The verified checkpoint loader currently approves only a hardcoded demo artifact digest and metadata; there is no generic signed candidate registry.
No automated production model promotion is configured; candidate acceptance is BLOCKED and production model slot is empty.
API middleware logs rounded location buckets; retention/privacy requirements should determine whether this telemetry is necessary.
Runtime API response schema validation is delegated to FastAPI response_model; failures are generic 500 but no dedicated response-contract test covers every endpoint.

limitations: No Git repository metadata is available.
Static source scanning does not establish absence of all vulnerabilities.
Binary raw dataset payloads and node_modules are excluded from secret text scanning; binary credential scanning was not performed.
Provider source claims, operational availability semantics, and deployment topology require owner verification.
